clue.text: Sign of distemper being difficult to apply to one's room

parts.note: difficult means hard
a pad is slang for the place where one lives, one's room or flat

explanation.surface: A vet notes that a dog's illness is making it hard to keep its quarters tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: HARDPAD is a hardening of a dog's footpads, a symptom of canine distemper. 'being' and 'to apply to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardpad is a thickening of the paw pads that is a classic symptom of canine distemper.

indicators.note: one piece keeps the other within it, so the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A substance that a single pupil has hidden away in the school building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps in' tells us the card word holds the school inside it. Eton College is England's best-known boarding school; 'one' as the top card is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a common organic solvent, so it is a chemical by example.

parts.note: seems to describe saliva or dribbling, but means the fan of river water and silt where a river meets the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the area of channels and deposited sediment at a river's mouth.

parts.note: seems to mean the angle or slope of a roof, but means the black tarry material used to cover one

explanation.surface: A builder asks how steeply a roof slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a bituminous pitch used as a waterproof covering on flat roofs.

clue.text: Pushing out a helicopter, for example

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A helicopter is being pushed out of a hangar.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed helicopter is a type of gunship, so the definition gives an example.

indicators.note: turn tells us to rearrange the letters of the rest of the word

explanation.surface: Reversals of policy are happening on board ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Turnabouts' splits as 'Turn' (the anagram signal) and 'abouts', whose letters rearrange to UBOATS.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines, a kind of naval vessel.

parts.note: seems to be a man out in a meadow, but guy means an effigy stuffed with straw, set up among crops

explanation.surface: Some fellow is standing out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is the stuffed effigy burnt on Bonfire Night in Britain, so a guy in a field is a figure set up to frighten birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a dressed-up straw figure, an effigy like a guy, placed among crops.

clue.text: Hostile incursions into Greek island, say

parts.note: into gives the short word in

indicators.note: say tells us the island's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Enemy raids are being made on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means RHODES is heard, giving ROADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile raids or advances into enemy territory.

clue.text: Make bet, say, with counters on what may be on the menu

definitions.text: what may be on the menu

indicators.note: say tells us the word for making a bet is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to make a bet is to stake money
with means and
chips are the counters used in gambling

explanation.surface: A gambler places a bet using casino counters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means STAKE is heard, giving STEAK. In Britain chips are what Americans call fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak and chips is a classic pub or restaurant dish, so it may well be on a menu.

definitions.meaning: A seaside town and former port in Kent, England
to trade, buy and sell

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a Kentish port town, and a deal is also a trading transaction or to trade.

clue.text: Plays records and is greatly affected

definitions.meaning: read literally, a DJ sets tunes playing on a turntable
behaves in a pretentious, haughty manner

explanation.definitionFit: To put on airs is an idiom for acting superior, and literally it means starting tunes playing.

clue.text: Issue a word of thanks for some music

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A child says thank you in return for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for 'thanks'. 'for' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, usually for one or two instruments.

definitions.meaning: in Britain barristers are called to the Bar, so they practise in the legal profession
standing at a pub counter having a drink

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both practising as a barrister and being at the counter of a pub.

clue.text: A vow to make both alter

indicators.note: make suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Getting engaged means both partners must change their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' signals the anagram of BOTH and ALTER together; 'to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is an engagement to marry, a mutual promise or vow.

clue.text: Recovery results in delight round the City

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: rapture is great delight
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: An economic upturn brings joy to the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' says the word for joy goes around the City, the financial district of London, whose postcode letters are a crossword staple. 'results in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Recapture is the act of getting something back, a recovery.

definitions.meaning: a collapse, as of a business or computer
a coarse linen fabric

explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden collapse, and crash is also a coarse fabric for towels.

clue.text: Cheat with cards and make a pile

definitions.meaning: to arrange a deck dishonestly
to heap things up

explanation.definitionFit: To stack a deck is to fix it dishonestly, and to stack things is to heap them.

clue.text: Its crew makes progress on three levels

definitions.text: Its crew makes progress on three levels

parts.words: Its crew makes progress on three levels
parts.note: sounds like a team advancing on several fronts, but describes oarsmen rowing from three banks of seats

explanation.surface: A team is advancing in three areas at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three tiers of rowers.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
swine means pig

explanation.surface: Someone fetches drinking water for a sow.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine is an old humorous phrase for plain water, the only drink Adam had.

clue.text: Master takes female, over 50, in marriage

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
Rita is a woman's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man weds a woman in her fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places RITA above L in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, as in marital bliss.

parts.note: a novel is a book
lo is an old word meaning see or look

explanation.surface: Someone books a ticket to see a star of stage and song.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh actor and songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a famous Welsh actor and composer of musicals.

clue.text: He remains in the running for a long time

definitions.text: He remains in the running for a long time

parts.words: He remains in the running for a long time
parts.note: sounds like a contender staying in a race, describes a horse or runner with stamina for long distances

explanation.surface: A candidate stays in contention for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or athlete with endurance for long races.

definitions.meaning: to send something on its way
an official report sent from abroad
speed, as in done with all due speed

explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch means to send off, a sent report, and promptness or speed.

definitions.meaning: to bare is to take off or strip away
Billy Bunter, the comic schoolboy of Greyfriars stories, was in the class of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Frank Richards's British school stories; his form was the Remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove is to strip away, and the Remove is the form Billy Bunter was in.

definitions.meaning: to wed
an archaic exclamation of surprise or emphasis, like indeed

explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to wed, and Marry! is an archaic oath meaning indeed.

clue.text: Boy upset at vandalised tourist attraction

indicators.note: vandalised suggests the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry lad has trashed a famous sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' signals the anagram of BOY, UPSET and AT; 'upset' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a place of scenic beauty that draws visitors.

definitions.meaning: control or authority
a ... is used to measure, and a ... is a measuring stick

explanation.definitionFit: Rule means governing authority and also a straight measuring rod.

clue.text: Possibly rely on clergyman for the festivities

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

indicators.note: possibly says the word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A vicar may be relied on for a church party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals the anagram of the printed word rely, and 'on' puts that shuffle after the clergyman's title. 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is merrymaking, the noisy celebration of festivities.

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who ... hits the ball onto his own stumps and is out
keeps playing, continues

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, playing on means deflecting the ball into one's own wicket, which gets the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays on is a cricket way of being out, and also means carries on.
